newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks drift at open, slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks drift at open, slow trade.

text.p: Australian shares opened narrowly mixed on Thursday with no strong signals from offshore markets to guide investors.
Turnover was light and was seen remaining that way with few local events to inspire traders.
At 10.20 a.m. (2320 GMT), the All Ordinaries index edged 1.6 points lower to 2,335.1.
"There is not much in it," said a Brisbane dealer. "The Dow was off a bit and the market is back in a quiet drift mode."
The dealer noted the Reserve Bank of Australia board meeting on November 5 and imminent U.S. elections, saying he expected little major drive in the market until after those events.
"There is nothing much doing. I think people have gone into neutral a little bit with the Reserve Bank meeting Tuesday and the U.S. elections," he said.
"People are not committing either way until we get an outcome from those things."
Rises and falls were level pegging, while about 50 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
